analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md, adding head lines 198-215: a 'Close codes and the reconnect wait' section. It documents that the provider reads only the WebSocket close code (not the reason) from the coordinator side. Code 1012 draws the wait from serviceRestartDelayRange without growing the backoff. Any other code, or no close frame, uses ExponentialBackoff, which grows. A session open for stableSessionDuration or longer, counted from its register frame, resets the backoff. Every reconnect sends a fresh register. The change is documentation only, with no code, key handling, attestation, encryption or authorization changes. The rest of the file is unchanged context.

Threat model relevance is limited to TB-002 (the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket) and availability. The coordinator is trusted, so a coordinator-sent 1012 only shortens the reconnect wait, bounded by serviceRestartDelayRange. The doc says the backoff does not grow on 1012, which is a mild reconnect-storm consideration. That is a design choice in CoordinatorReconnectPolicy, which was not supplied, and the doc does not claim an unbounded value. The statement that every reconnect sends a fresh register is consistent with the endpoint-resumption section, which creates a fresh nonce per NWConnection, and with the drain text saying a restart registers and authorizes a new connection. I identified no weakening of the existing text on App Attest, resume, drain or the add-on hold. The doc makes no claim that reconnect grants trust or authorization.

Remaining unverified: the actual CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift behavior and the values of serviceRestartDelayRange and stableSessionDuration were not supplied. The cli-reference runtime-constants anchor was not checked, so doc/code consistency is unconfirmed. This is not a security regression.
